### Populus
<note>Populus, Latin for "The People," is a geomantic figure represented by two vertical lines of two dots. It signifies crowds, movement, passivity, and reflection of its surroundings.</note>

**Populus** signifies those with "double hearts" <note>original: *duplice cordib*, implying fickle or indecisive natures</note> who are more inclined toward delight in good than in evil; a weak honor, a doubtful status, and movement from place to place. It represents a multitude of things and actions, many of which are grand and lasting. It relates to a matter like war, which involves many men for some grand purpose (such as for bishops or for the pleasure of the many). It signifies the movement of water, a doubtful change of a grand place, a will that is fulfilled, the "night" of a matter, a vile hand, a predecessor of light, and one fearful of prophecy because the person is lowly and fading. 

<margin>¶</margin> **In the second part** <note>The 2nd house concerns wealth, possessions, and resources.</note> it signifies a wandering and moderate fortune, small profit, and many mobile things. That which is quieted is neither preferred nor does it bring honors, family, or service. It indicates a quickly changing good, gain, service, and the acquisition of a bitter thing or something against one's will, following the path of merchants (which primarily concerns kings and doctors). 

<margin>¶</margin> **In the 3rd house** <note>The 3rd house concerns siblings, short journeys, and messages.</note> many paths and quieted honors; a fast change; a letter <note>original: *missiua*</note> sent from a loved one <note>original: *ayatā*, possibly a Latinization of the Arabic *hayat*, meaning "life" or a term of endearment</note>; a quieted good among many powerful things or thefts; the delight of them; the acquisition of a desired thing through the spirit of truth or power. 

<margin>¶</margin> **In the present [house]** <note>Likely continuing the 3rd house themes.</note> it signifies the love of brothers and sisters, which is like dust—vain—and the same regarding rumors and a moderate darkness. 

<margin>¶</margin> **In the 4th house** <note>The 4th house concerns the father, the home, and the "end of the matter."</note> a doubtful matter, a double inheritance, a place of many doubts, and a mediocre status. Many past things are to be taken as houses and waters; it signifies a good thing without doubt, and more good than evil; the movement of things, a hidden matter, agriculture, and good forests. 

<margin>¶</margin> **In the 5th house** <note>The 5th house concerns children, pleasure, and creativity.</note> many sons and daughters, goodness of heart, fast messengers, an exit, many friends or many houses. The matter pleases many; many wars in joy, or many drinks, or many falls of others; a doubtful promise. 

<margin>¶</margin> **In the 6th house** <note>The 6th house concerns illness, servants, and small animals.</note> a path or a moderate illness; moderate services; quieted and servile fears; the dread of servants; a good thing... many approaching rumors.

<summary>This page concludes the negative, restrictive interpretations of the geomantic figure Carcer and introduces Populus, which characterizes situations involving crowds, movement, and fluctuating fortunes across the first six houses.</summary>

<margin>¶</margin> **In the 14th house** <note>The 14th house is the Second Witness, representing the external environment or the "other."</note> it signifies many doubtful matters and double-speech <note>original: *sermo̅e duplice̅*, suggesting duplicity or ambiguity</note>, as well as true things coming from far away. <margin>¶</margin> **In the 15th house** <note>The 15th house is the Judge, providing the final outcome of the reading.</note> it signifies an end with a double understanding <note>original: *duplice i̅ tellectu̅*</note>, which is either weak or quite strong.

### Via
<note>Via, Latin for "The Way" or "The Path," is a geomantic figure consisting of four single dots in a vertical line. It represents movement, change, and sometimes instability or loneliness.</note>

**Via**, in the first house <note>The 1st house represents the life and person of the questioner.</note>, signifies life and the path of many from place to place. It suggests safety, yet in a weak state, along with poverty and doubtful fear in the heart. It indicates a messenger from the presence of the father, bringing news of infirmity, and a weak limit that passes away.

<margin>¶</margin> **In the 2nd house** <note>The 2nd house governs money, possessions, and personal values.</note> it signifies either a little gain or much loss to be received quickly. It suggests frivolous pacts, infirmity, and few goods. It reflects the truth of a pleasing thing and good things to come. It may indicate useful gain through theft, or the prediction of a certain matter, a pact, or the cause of a loss.

¶ **In the 12th house** <note>The 12th house traditionally governs hidden enemies, imprisonment, and sorrow.</note> [The Way] signifies small power of enemies, fewness, escape, and care regarding a late silence of a place—such as from the fatherland; a light death, a small loss of servants, and few other weak things are accomplished. ¶ **In the 13th house** <note>original: "In xiii f'e"; the 13th figure is the "Witness of the Past," representing the background of the query.</note> it signifies a retardation of life, or a life [led] after some lordly manner. It indicates a mutation coming from the death of lost things, and a lordship of great value, yet certainly a temperable doubt.

¶ **In the 14th house** <note>original: "In xiiii f'e"; the 14th figure is the "Witness of the Future," representing what comes next.</note> it signifies a prediction of a matter that is partly doubtful in fortune; certainly, it refers to a rapid mutation of what is held.

¶ **In the 15th house** <note>original: "In xv f'e"; the 15th figure is the "Judge," providing the final verdict of the geomantic reading.</note> it signifies a weak and doubtful end, a healthy escape, a mind easily occupied by such a change of will and purpose, and a rapid change of honor or of the fatherland. — **Here ends the third part of the book.**

If a question is proposed concerning the **state of someone's body** <note>original: "statu corporis"; this refers to general health, physical condition, or social standing.</note> whether it ought to be improved or not: Look at the first figure and the second for the past, and let the answers be applied. If the first or second figure is good and **fixed** <note>A "fixed" figure is one that suggests stability and lack of movement, such as "Fortuna Major."</note> and not removed from its place, it is said that the person's status is quiet, good, firm, and will remain so for a long time. It is said that their state ought not to deteriorate at all in the matter you wish to know.

¶ If the figures should be **mobile** <note>original: "generium," likely referring to "general" or "moving/mobile" figures like Via or Albus.</note> instead of fixed, the figures in this edition indicate—through the lord who governs the first figure and the one found remaining in the place—whether there is a mutation of the house or place. If the first is good and fixed, and a good figure is applied to it, then the state will change for some reason, yet it signifies that the seeker will prevail well for a long time in that same state.

¶ And if the first figure is good and fixed, and not changed from its place, and yet a corrupted or mutated and disordered figure is applied to it, then the answer is that the status will not change for a long time; however, in the course of fortune it will deteriorate and change, as that figure naturally holds an evil sign.

¶ Also, if the first figure is good and fixed, but it moves itself into another place—as into the fourth [house] or in the way <note>original: "in via"; referring either to the 15th house or the general "path" of the reading.</note>, or in the sixth or eleventh house—the answer is that the state will be improved altogether from its non-good [condition], and it will be changed for the better by the person themselves or through those who are not present in the places where the mutation occurred.

¶ But if it moves more strongly, it is transformed.

# The First House
<note>original: "pma dom⁹" / "Prima Domus". In geomancy and astrology, the First House represents the individual, their physical body, and the beginning of all things.</note>

**Figure 1.** If it falls quickly <note>meaning it is a "mobile" or fast-moving figure</note>, it signifies pain or even death unless a remedy is made through certain figures such as *becharig*, *rcharig*, or *ruffiang* <note>These appear to be technical, possibly Arabic-derived names for specific geomantic configurations</note>, or if one makes an agreement with one of the lords, or practices a unique art for their own benefit. 

If it reaches the world <note>original: "ad mundum"; likely referring to the earthly or physical realm of the chart</note> in the **Third House**, it signifies a religious disposition, such as a monk or a pilgrim, or a world of faith and a time of worship, such as the cult of God or of Muhammad <note>original: "machometi"; the text acknowledges different religious contexts for the querent</note>. 

If it reaches the **Tenth House** <note>original: "in X"; the house of career, honors, and public life</note>, it signifies reaching some lord or master for the sake of honor or gain, whether that master be a layman or a member of the clergy, or for the sake of two years. 

If it falls in the **Eleventh House** <note>original: "in XI"; the house of friends and hopes</note>, it will bring good fortune with a partner, a friend, or through something holy belonging to a lord, or one may even become holy themselves and profit much if the figure is favorable. 

If it reaches the **Twelfth House** <note>original: "in XII"; the house of hidden enemies and misfortune</note>, it signifies loss or damage, as mentioned before, such as through debtors, prisons, or lingering illnesses leading toward death, or the care of the poor who are in misery, such as in a hospice or hospital, or that one might die in such a place.

If the point is **fixed** <term>fixed</term><note>A geomantic figure is "fixed" if its structure suggests stability and permanence, rather than change.</note>, it signifies a long life from the first day in that place, or for one born in a certain garden of work and memory. And if it is **mobile**, everything it signifies will change or pass away quickly to its own state; this will be the nature of the figure in the first place. And if it should be of a variable form, it moves quickly from one place or part to another, and from that to another, according to its own motion. For these places which I have predicted are varied by the strength of the figures.

If the points are **masculine** and **bad**, such as:
<image-desc>Four geomantic figures: 1. Laetitia (Joy), 2. Albus (White), 3. Rubeus (Red), 4. Puer (The Boy)</image-desc>
it is a sign that it pertains more to men than to women, and to boldness and the weapons which they carry. 

But if they are **feminine**, such as:
<image-desc>Four geomantic figures: 1. Tristitia (Sorrow), 2. Albus (White), 3. Rubeus (Red), 4. Laetitia (Joy)</image-desc>
all the things predicted relate to a delay with women, with voices, and with manners, being more or less than what was said before, because the figure would lead to a pleasing state below.

## Calculating the Length of Life

If it is asked how many years a person will live from their birth, see how the figure proceeds. To see if it is much or little, look at the first part of the earth <note>likely the First House or the base of the figure</note> and count how many units <note>points</note> it carries. For every unit, the person shall live or remain in that state for so many hours, or days, or weeks, or months, or years, according to the current condition. This is according to the parts mentioned above and the chapter handed down. If it falls in another way, I hope for honor. If however it falls in the **Tenth**, it acts as a rewarder, because that first part is divided into four, and then into fourteen. If the question was about the points, then the number of the "sons" <term>filii</term><note>The "Sons" are the second set of four figures generated in a geomantic chart.</note> or the "hundreds" <note>original: "c"; Roman numeral for 100</note> shows the house in which it now resides.

### First House
<note>original: "dom^9 p^ma" refers to the First House in a geomantic chart, which represents the querent (the person asking) and their beginnings.</note>

<image-desc>red cross-like decorative mark</image-desc>

If it is asked in which month someone was born when they do not know this: look at the **First Parent** <note>The "First Parent" is the first of four primary figures drawn to start a geomantic chart.</note> and the matter requested. For according to whatever the figure of the sign of the month may be, judge him to have been born either at the beginning or at the end of those days. Add the whole measure to the outcome. For example, if **Gain** <note>original: "Acquisitio", geomantic figure: 2-1-2-1</note> is in the first house, since it is the figure of **Taurus** and of the first part of the month, it should be said that his birth was in the first days of **April**. And it is judged thus because **Gain** <image-desc>geomantic figure of six red dots in a 2-1-2-1 pattern (Acquisitio)</image-desc> and **Greater Fortune** <image-desc>geomantic figure of six red dots in a 2-2-1-1 pattern (Fortuna Major)</image-desc> are the figures of the month of **April** and the sign of **Taurus**. And so it proceeds in order through all the months and signs. For if **The People** <note>original: "Populus", geomantic figure: 2-2-2-2</note> is in the first house, since it is the sign of **Aries**, and **Aries** is the sign for the month of **March**, judge the birth to have been in **March**. 

Furthermore, if the first figure has not moved <note>In geomancy, figures "move" or pass from one house to another to show how an influence develops.</note>, say his birth was in the month of **January**, since it is the first month; however, it is better to say that it is the month whose nature the figure itself possesses, which the first figure makes known in the designated form. But if it has moved, see the place of birth <note>the house it moved to</note> and according to that, you can judge more reasonably. For example, if **White** <note>original: "Albus", geomantic figure: 2-2-1-2</note> <image-desc>geomantic figure of five red dots in a 1-2-1-1 pattern (Albus)</image-desc> in the first house moves into the third house <note>original: "t_er_am"</note>, judge it to be the first month, either **January** or **April**, which the first figure indicates; and so judge the beginning, middle, or end, according to how the figure is proved to be in the signs and months. 

But if the first figure has moved into the third house <note>original: "t_er_am do^"</note>, say it was in the third month from the first—that is, in **March**, and so on. Regarding the full assignment <note>original: "De ant plena"</note>, we speak according to the figures written below:

If it is asked in which week of the month someone was born: look at the **First Parent** and the matter requested. For if the first was not moved from its place <note>stayed in the First House</note>, whatever the sign or planet may be, say it was in the **first week**. If, however, it was moved from its place, then judge according to the place of its motion. For if it was in the second house, say the **second week**. If in the third house, say the **third**. If in the fourth house, say the **fourth**. If in the fifth, say the **first week** of the following month, and so on, since a month does not have more than four weeks. And thus, if it was in the sixth house, say the first week of that month; if in the seventh house, the third week; if you wish, say the fourth week, and so on.

**I**f you wish to know the hidden intention of those who come to you to speak with you about any matter—whether the time for that thing is good or bad—and also whether it is a single matter, or if they come to you to test you or to seek the Art concerning some necessity: look at the preliminary inquiry of the matter sought. If, however, the figures should be **mobile** <term>mobile figure: a geomantic sign associated with change and speed, like Fortuna Minor</term> and **masculine** <note>In geomancy, signs are gendered; masculine signs are generally considered more active or assertive</note>, it pronounces that one should speak favorably. But if they are **common** <term>common figure: also called "mutable," these signs indicate a mix of stability and change</term> and masculine, they signify that the matter is partly true and partly false. The opposite, however, signifies the opposite of what was said before; that is, if the signs of the places of the gods should be **feminine** and **bad** <note>original: "male," referring to "malefic" or unfavorable figures</note>, whether they be fixed, mobile, or common—just as it is useful for anyone to <unclear>change</unclear> into the aforementioned places—it is a sign that what is being said is false.

And if the aforementioned place was not merely **fixed** <term>fixed figure: a stable, slow-moving sign like Fortuna Major</term>, but has mobility such as being masculine, and is not removed from its place but is located in a good place, it says that the rumor is true, according to what has already been said somewhere in those locations. If it is masculine and good, and elsewhere feminine and bad—since some are fixed and some mobile—as with common figures, it is partly doubtful and partly false. Regarding the said rumor, there is more truth and more falsehood according to whether the greater part of the figures placed in those locations is of daily goodness or malice, and so on.

Again, 
we say this same thing according to the testimony of the **four angles** <term>four angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a geomantic chart, representing the pillars of the sky and the most powerful positions</term> received and indicated by the five principal figures of the matter, namely the **1st, 11th, 7th, and 8th** houses. If good and masculine figures are found in those places, whatever might have been in the others, it signifies the absolute truth of the matter at its root; if they are bad, they signify falsehood. They hold, however, by concession, that the locations of the figure verify a rumor to be true regarding something good, or bad regarding something evil. The reason is because they are generated according to their innate nature and the natures joined to them. One must consider the subject matter about which the rumor is heard. For if the rumor is about something good and the figure's location is similarly [good], it pronounces the truth regarding the favorable nature of the question; then it is a sign that the rumor about it is true. And if it is about something bad and the figures are bad, then it is a sign that the rumor of all those things is true. Or the opinion is this: whether the rumor is about something good or bad, if the figure is masculine and the aforementioned place is good, it affirms it is true. Feminine and bad figures, however, deny it entirely, a distinction which some do not observe.

If one asks whether it be true or false what is said about such a matter, or what someone said or presupposed, or whether he communicated it or not—or even if he says or presumes it to happen, such as **whether the Pope is now in Rome** <note>A common medieval example used to test the accuracy of a divination</note>, or if such a pilgrimage is in such a house as if <unclear>traveling</unclear> there still or not, or **whether treasure is in such a place** or not: It is seen through the **11th, 7th, and 8th** parts of the question. For if the "voice" is thus in the said places and represents more masculine figures to which it returns a good exposition, and the **four angles** and the **Index** <term>Index: a figure derived during the calculation of a geomantic chart, used to help reach the final "Judge" or verdict</term> precede as the majority part, it is a sign that it is so.

### On Changes of Location and Travel

.1. If it is asked whether a matter shall come to pass, such as a change from place to place, it appears one should first inquire at the place in which the subject stays, which is the **Eleventh House** <note>original: *11a*; while often the house of hopes, in this context it is used to locate the person being asked about</note>. If the inquiry concerns the physical person, look to the **Seventh House**; if the place is known or unknown, look to the **Ninth House**. If indeed... <insert>¶</insert> If the **First Figure** <term>First Figure: The figure representing the person asking the question (the querent).</term> is **mobile** <term>mobile figure: Figures like *Via* (Way) or *Conjunctio* (Conjunction) that suggest movement and rapid change.</term>, as for those who are not far from a place but have changed their circumstances, it is a sign that movement will occur entirely and will happen very quickly.

Whence it is that if the **First Figure** is mobile, as it may have been previously, it is better or more likely that it has changed. It is a sign that a change from place to place will happen quickly, and one which does not result in a return. Conversely, if the figure is **fixed** <term>fixed figure: Figures like *Carcer* (Prison) or *Acquisitio* (Gain) that suggest stability, staying in place, or delay.</term>, then there is no change of location. If the figure is good and shows a change of place, then that change will be good and will proceed fairly. <insert>¶</insert> And if it is good, then it ought to appear well and proceed freely.

<insert>¶</insert> If the **First House** is such that the **Third**, **Ninth**, or **Eleventh Houses** are similarly found to have changed, it is a sign of movement, and it will happen quickly. For if the **Third House** <note>The house of short journeys.</note> is involved, the change will happen by land; but if it is the **Twelfth** or **Ninth** <note>The house of long journeys.</note>, the destination is far away. <insert>¶</insert> But if the **Twelfth** or **First** indicates a long distance, and the figure in that house is fixed, it is a sign that he does not return from that place and will not move from that location to inhabit other regions.

<insert>¶</insert> If indeed the figure was mobile, then he will change for the better or more; it is a sign that he will change entirely, but he will delay much according to the slow motion of the stars or for some other cause. <insert>¶</insert> So it is that if the nature of the figure is fixed, it holds its signs... its effect is as if it were mobile, however quickly it may move. <insert>¶</insert> If the **Three Angles** <term>Angles: Also called 'cardines' or hinges; these are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, representing the strongest points of influence in a chart.</term> are fixed, they signify great delay in movements. Or they may not show the outcome clearly in the demonstrations. 

But according to the mobile figures, they move with speed. <insert>¶</insert> And if some of them are fixed and others are mobile, it is a sign that first a movement will occur by traveling to another region, but not in the way the journey was perhaps first thought of or ordered; thereafter let another thing be considered and then ordered.

If it is asked whether things ought to happen by land or by water, every change seems to ought to happen before a year or within one year. Then look indeed at the **Eleventh** and **Ninth Houses**. <insert>¶</insert> And if the figures of those places are **Watery** <note>original: *aquae*; geomantic figures are associated with the four elements: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth. Watery figures include *Populus* and *Via*.</note>, it is a sign that the journey will be made by water. <insert>¶</insert> If indeed the figure is of **Earth**, it is by land, as noted above. If it is of **Air**, then it will happen through the air, or as if in a ship led through fresh or salt water. <insert>¶</insert> In this, truly see the principles...

### **I**f it be asked whether a treasure is contained in a certain place, such as a house, or whether it can be found and possessed:

Look at the first questioner in the **Second, Third, Seventh, Eighth, Eleventh, and Twelfth** houses <note>The "houses" here refer to the twelve positions in a geomantic chart, mirroring astrological houses</note> that have been skillfully placed. For if, in the indeterminate whole or in the greater part, the figure is good, it signifies the discovery and possession of the hidden thing. And if the first figure was good, as previously mentioned, and fortunate, let it be found in the **Second House**, and so it is said concerning the "translation" <note>original: "t’nslatōīo," an astrological term where a faster planet or figure moves between two others, "carrying" the influence from one to the other</note>, as a good occupation of the property. And if in the **Third House** the angles were good, either in the whole or in the greater part, by which they return a good result, then judge by the first receptions. The same is said for a fortunate outcome, which signifies that success depends on this. And first, in the **Third House**, one asks whether it is truly good, and so forth.

### **I**f it be asked concerning the substance and color of the hidden treasure in the found place:

Look at the first question, and the **Second, Third, Fifth, Seventh, and Eleventh** parts. Through these, the same element that more abounds shall possess the place. For as for the color: 

If the figure is of **Earth** <note>original: "t’reā"</note>, it signifies **iron, lead, stone, a gemstone, or bodies** that are fashioned and cooked by fire, such as **bricks, tiles, and boundary stones**, or the rust of metal, etc. 

A figure of **Water** signifies a **white thing** and especially **liquid and moist gold** <note>original: "aurū lī dā," likely referring to mercury or "white gold"</note> that is not very clear, like **honey, balsam, gum, oil**, etc. 

A figure of **Air** signifies a **green thing**, or **white, or violet**, etc. 

A figure of **Fire** signifies a **red thing or saffron-colored**, such as **gold, saffron**, etc. Truly, there is no great power or necessity to know this except by necessity.

If it be asked to what end and of what kind a man might arrive concerning a matter in which he currently is, or which is to be begun, look to the first [house] <note>The "First House" in geomancy represents the person asking the question and the beginning of the matter.</note> providing the beginning as it proceeds in its trials; then afterward, do the same with the 3rd and the 2nd; and the 11th for fortune. In the 2nd and 11th, the matter to be finished is searched for through the ultimate result; the 10th for honor; and the 4th, which is the end of the matter. For if in the said places there should be good figures, strong and masculine <note>In geomancy, figures are categorized as masculine or feminine, which dictates their "active" or "passive" strength.</note> in their entirety, then in the greater part they will be good and fortunate; say this same thing [of the outcome]. If, however, some of them were good and some evil—or some are firm and some removed from their places—then you shall judge the end of the matter by the condition of the houses and locations.

Doing this: if the first [figure] was **Gain** <image-desc>geomantic figure: Acquisitio</image-desc> it is good; and if **Joy** <image-desc>geomantic figure: Laetitia</image-desc> is better, then it follows that if it is in the 4th, it is likewise good. It is a sign of a good beginning and a better end. Equally, if such a figure was in the 4th as was in the 1st, it signifies that the end shall be of the same kind as the beginning was or shall be. And if one of them was worse than the other, you shall judge that they are in a state of difference. For example, if you compare the beginning and the end of these: if **Greater Fortune** <image-desc>geomantic figure: Fortuna Major</image-desc> was better than the 1st and the 4th, it signifies that the middle [of the affair] will be better than the beginning and the end, and there will be more honor from fame than utility, and so on. Likewise, if there are better figures in the <term>succedent houses</term> <note>Succedent houses (2, 5, 8, 11) follow the "angles" and represent resources and stability.</note> than in the <term>angles</term> <note>The Angles (1, 4, 7, 10) are the most powerful positions in a chart.</note>, there will be more utility than is believed, and better fortune than power in matters, as in depth and cause. ### On the state of a city

If a question is asked concerning the state of a city <note>original: "statu civitate"</note>, such as whether it is currently in a good state, one should look at the 1st and 4th [houses], and for the state of the mind <note>original: "mentem"</note> the 7th; the 4th house specifically reveals the state of the matter and the state of its people. For if the 1st and 4th houses contain good figures that are fixed <note>Figures in geomancy are classified as "fixed" (stable), "mobile" (changing), or "common" (variable).</note> and fortunate, and not removed from their proper places, say that city is entirely in a good, firm state and will be preserved so for a long time. 

But if they are changeable; and equally if only the 4th house contained a good, fixed, and fortunate figure not removed from its place, it signifies the same. And if the figure was moved into a "good" house, it signifies the same. If, however, it was moved into an "evil" house, say that the city is currently in a good state and will be preserved so for a long time, but afterward it will fall into an evil state. 

And if both figures were mobile or of any other kind—whether good or without an "evil line"—then you should say to the seeker that the city is in a good state for the present, but it will not be preserved so for long; its state will deteriorate and multiply. It is near to a fall from heaven <note>original: "celi casu," implying a loss of celestial favor or a sudden decline</note> or a change from one state to another, which ought to be judged by the quality of the figures regarding the change of place. It is true that this sign also comes about through whatever figures, as much through mobile ones as through fixed ones of the elements of Fire and Air, rather than through any other element. 

If, however, the 1st house is very dissimilar to the 4th, such that one is fixed and the other mobile, or if one is of one element and the other of another, then it is a sign that it is not in a firm state, but in a state of doubtful preservation. And if in the 1st or in the 4th, or in both houses, there were an evil figure such as **The Girl** <image-desc>geomantic figure Puella: one dot, two dots, one dot, one dot</image-desc> or **The Boy** <image-desc>geomantic figure Puer: one dot, one dot, two dots, one dot</image-desc> <note>While usually positive or neutral, the author here classifies these figures as "evil" or unfavorable in the context of the city's stability.</note>, speak securely of its downfall.

**If** one asks about some inheritance that is contested between two strangers, and the inheritance itself seems to belong to them by way of a legacy or through a donation made <term>inter vivos<note>original: "in vivo[rum]"; a legal term referring to a gift or transfer made during the donor's lifetime.</note></term>, you must know which of them will obtain it. But if both figures should be equal and firm in their places, it is a sign of agreement between them, so that neither will obtain it for a certain time; look then to the sixth house and the fourth to see which side is more impoverished.

**If** one asks about the purchase of any immovable thing, such as a house or a castle, whether it will be useful or useless to the buyer: Look to the first house for the seeker, the fourth for the thing being sold, the seventh for the seller, and the ninth, eleventh, sixteenth, and fourteenth <note>The manuscript uses abbreviated Roman numerals here; these houses typically relate to profit, luck, and the final outcome.</note> for the profit and the fortune of the profit from this thing. Likewise, if the first was good and is found repeated in the fourth, or in its company before or after it, this signifies a good end. If the sixteenth and eighteenth <note>original: "xvj xvijij," likely referring to the final summary figures of the geomantic shield.</note> were good and fortunate, it is an indication of the goodness of the profit and utility. Not only should you look at the <term>angles<note>The "angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in any divination chart.</note></term>, but if the index <note>The "index" or judge is the final figure that summarizes the chart.</note> in its entirety or in its greater part was good, the same outcome is signified for him. **If** one asks whether the present year ought to be prosperous in terms of food supplies and a good market, or if it will not be, or if he wants to know about the coming year: how it will be, whether hot or cold, dry or windy, humid or calm. Furthermore, it should be known that if there were fiery figures in the said places, it signifies heat and dryness.

If a question is asked regarding the year, then in this manner more is attributed to one month than to another, and not otherwise than according to the intention the seeker chose. Whence, just as the year is divided into four seasons <note>original: "etates" (ages/seasons)</note> or the life of men is likewise divided, so it is done for the month and in similar fashion. **S**i a question is asked concerning the sowing of any matter, whether it be for the planting of a herb or a tree—if it should be done now so that in such a time it might reach perfection or not, or abound in its fruit—look first to the 1st house <note>original: "m" for matrem (mother), the house of the querent</note> and the 10th house <note>original: "cā" for cauda/caput or the 'angle' representing the business or goal</note>. ### On the Color of Clothing

If it is asked what color a promised garment will be, look to the 1st house for the seeker and the house representing the thing sought <note>usually the 2nd or 3rd house for movable goods</note>. For according to the significance of the colors of the figures, the color of the clothing is told. It is true that if the 1st house contains the same figure, it signifies that color.
<margin>o</margin>
And if the element of the 1st house abounds more than that of the house of the thing sought, the color will be such as the 1st signifies. But if they are dissimilar figures, the color is designated either by a **mixture** of the two or by the internal mixture of the figure itself.

If one asks about the colors of fabrics for a man who consults the fortune of his lord in order to dress himself in new clothes, look to the 1st and 4th houses, as well as the 2nd, 3rd, 7th, and 11th. The 3rd house specifically signifies the garment. 

For whichever figure abounds most throughout the entire question demonstrates the natural color of its **planet** and **element** more than the others. It is true that every figure represents the fortune of its own color in its place, which it naturally signifies through its planet and element. Therefore, one must see which figure abounds most in those houses with its element and planet, or where multiple figures appear to give a unified judgment. In a question where there are diverse figures in the houses, they designate a mixture of colors; or, there are as many fortunate colors for dressing oneself as there are various figures in the houses. For example, the **element of fire** naturally signifies a **red color like blood**.

### On a Fugitive or Absent Son

**I**f a question is asked concerning someone’s fugitive son, or one who is absent while his family is ignorant of his state—whether he is hidden, or led away, or staying somewhere, or whether he ought to ever return home or not: Look to the **1st house** for the seeker (such as a mother or father), and the **5th house** for the son, the **7th house** for the fugitive, and the **8th house** for the absent one. Also the **9th house**, for if in these same places there should be good, **mobile** <term>Mobile figures (composed mostly of single dots) indicate rapid movement or change.</term> figures of mobile elements, and they are not removed from the location, it is a sign that he will return quickly. 

If the figure of the son is found in a certain house, such as in the **3rd** or **5th**, it signifies either that he will send news or a slow messenger. If the figure moves from one body <note>meaning the figure repeats or "passes" from one house to another</note> above the **4th** and **5th** houses into any other part, he is governing himself or spending time in those places; then he does not signify his own return. This is done because the transition of the figures through a complete view or pronunciation—or as an occupation, perfection, junction, or similar conjunction—can happen either quickly or slowly depending on the projection of the principal figures. For **fixed** figures <term>Fixed figures (composed mostly of double dots) indicate stability, delay, or staying put.</term> delay the outcome, while **mobile** ones accelerate the effect. 

If the figure in the **1st**, **7th**, or **5th** house moves into the part of the **4th** mother <note>The "Mothers" are the first four figures created in a geomantic chart</note>, it is a sign that he will return and will not stay long in the place where he changed, because he has moved himself like a figure. And if the figure from the **1st**, **2nd**, **5th**, **7th**, or **8th** house moves into the **12th house** <note>The house of imprisonment, hidden enemies, and sorrow</note>, it is a sign that he will never return, and especially in this time—that is, not quickly. If the **Witnesses** <note>original: "anglī respectuʳ"; likely the "testimony" of the final figures in the chart</note> in respect to the whole or the better part are good and firm in their movement, and yet the figure moves into a bad place, it signifies the same for him; and it is similar regarding the aforementioned journey.

### On the Status and Health of the Absent

**I**f a question is asked concerning the state or health of someone who is absent or far away from the seeker’s home—namely, whether such a person is healthy or infirm, joyful or sad, rich or poor: Look to the **1st house** for the seeker <gloss>1</gloss>, the **5th house** for the relationship to the son <gloss>2</gloss>, the **2nd house** for his movable substance and family <gloss>3</gloss>, the **8th house** for the absent <gloss>⁊</gloss> <note>and</note>, and the **11th house** <gloss>4</gloss> for the thing in which there is trust and the fulfillment of health. For if in these same places there should be good figures in the inspection of **Fortune**, and they are not in remote places, and do not afterward move into a bad place, it speaks well of his state.

### On the Freedom of Servants

If it is asked whether a manservant or maidservant is bound to his lordship forever, or until a certain time when he shall be freed <note>original: "franciscetur," referring to enfranchisement or granting of 'franchise' (freedom)</note> or not. For if in two places there are good figures and they are concordant in the greater part or in the whole, it signifies good on his part, because he is seen to come to himself through his freedom in his own time. <note>Red paragraph marker</note> And if the 6th or 12th houses are good and are found in the 1st or 4th, it signifies the same; and conversely, if the principal figures are discordant in their members <term>membris: the individual points that make up a geomantic figure</term> within themselves, you will find another result most of all. You shall judge the species in both kinds. <note>Red paragraph marker</note> and it is to be known that if the aforesaid figures are fixed <term>fixe: geomantic figures associated with stability and permanence</term>, neither remote nor similar to each other, then it is a sign that he will not be manumitted <term>manumittetur: the formal legal process of freeing a slave</term> from the lordship. If, however, they are mobile <term>mobiles: figures associated with change and movement</term> or common, then it signifies that he was often moved by words of freedom; when he shall complete that which is fulfilled in the end, it is near for that time, whereas with fixed figures it is delayed.

Likewise, the herb named below, called **Blessed Thistle** <note>original: *Cardo benedictus*; a Mediterranean plant (*Centaurea benedicta*) once considered a "cure-all" in medieval Europe.</note>, was brought by Emperor Frederick from <unclear>Trier</unclear> <note>original: *trierth*; possibly referring to Trier, or perhaps a corruption of Damietta or another crusader site.</note> and came from India, and it has within it these written virtues and powers:

Likewise, whoever eats of this herb shall be relieved of many afflictions, especially that which comes above the eyes called **"the nail"** <note>original: *der nagel*; a historical term for a piercing, localized headache or migraine that feels as though a nail is being driven into the head.</note>, which makes him feel as though a nail were being struck through his head.

## The Golden Water

Also, take first three **farthings** <term>fierling: a quarter-pound unit of weight</term> of the noble sage, 2 **lots** <term>lot: approx. 15 grams or half an ounce</term> of nutmeg, 1 lot of cloves, 2 lots of ginger, 2 lots of cinnamon, 1 lot of **grains of paradise** <note>original: "paris körner"; a spicy seed from West Africa related to ginger</note>, 1 **quint** <term>quint: a small weight, usually 1/4 of a lot</term> of sugar, 1 quint of **olive oil** <note>original: "bömol"; literally "tree oil"</note>, 1 lot of **bitter apples** <note>original: "iuden öpfel", literally "Jewish apples"; the purgative fruit of the colocynth vine</note>, 2 lots of lavender, 1 quint of noble cloves, 1 quint of **zedoary** <note>original: "zytwen"; an aromatic root similar to turmeric</note>, 1 lot of laurel, 1 lot of cardamom, 1 quint of pennyroyal, 1 quint of **calamint** <note>original: "dewmenten"; wild mint</note>, 1 quint of wormwood, 1 quint of hyssop, 1 quint of borage flowers, 1 quint of **masterwort** <note>original: "hertwurz"; used historically for various heart and respiratory conditions</note>, 1 lot of galangal, 1 lot of rosemary, 2 lots of lemon balm, 1 lot of long pepper, and 1 lot of **manna** <note>a sweet plant resin used as a mild laxative</note>. Put all the roots and herbs together into three **measures** <note>original: "maß"; a standard liquid volume, roughly 1 to 1.5 liters</note> of the best wine you can obtain, and ensure there is six times more wine than all the roots combined. Let them lie therein and place it in a cellar for eight days; seal the jug well so that no **spirit** <term>spiritus: the volatile alcoholic essence</term> escapes from it. Afterward, draw the wine off from the roots and press them through a **fine cloth** <note>original: "pfīn důch"</note>, then pound the roots well in a mortar until they become soft. Then put them back into the wine and **distill** <note>original: "bren"; literally 'burn', the common term for distillation</note> it all together in a **distillation hood** <note>original: "roshůt"; literally a "horse-hat," describing the shape of the alembic's head</note>. And before it is finished distilling, place one lot of fresh sage into the water that has been distilled out; keep this in its full strength.

<meta>This page transitions from the medicinal recipes of the previous page (the Holy Oil and Golden Water) into the theoretical and practical foundations of the occult sciences, specifically the relationship between Astrology, Astronomy, and Geomancy.</meta>

Astrology is established upon the most noble art of geomancy as its foundation. In its grammar, the "matter" is established through proof; the "end" is the effect. The "form" of its principle is superior to physics. Its "office" <note>original: "offitium"; referring to the specific function or duty of the art</note> pertains to the time and the order in which its structures must be learned.

Geomancy is a certain art of divination. Therefore, its definition is established by the argument of its essence, approved through its three parts. Its "matter" consists of points; without matter, it moves toward that which it signifies. Its fourth matter is the earth, such as sand, which serves as the material for this work. Its "points" are the small particles that signify power, and the "third sign" and their motion serve the "end," which is to foretell the past and the future.

The "Efficient Cause" <note>A Scholastic term referring to the primary source of change or rest; the "agent" of the art.</note> of this art is found in its principles, which instruct the student in its teachings. Its "form" is perfected by linear points made in the proper matter. Through its application, geomancy is an art that clearly and diligently instructs the seeker <note>original: "gnatos"; likely referring to the "sons" or initiates of the art</note> regarding movement. Its "instruments" are the book of the art, earth, sand, paper, or wax tablets. To perform the work properly, sand should be gathered near a virgin before the sun rises, following the specific method of the place where the works are to be conducted.

Astronomy must be learned through astronomy because its "points" pertain to its structures, and the difficulty of astronomy is expressed within geomancy. The name is derived from "Geo," which is earth, and "manteia," which is divination—essentially "divination by earth" <note>The original OCR reads "macros," a likely scribal error for the Greek "manteia."</note>.

However, so that every judgment may be made worthily and with certainty, one must first consider the nature of the question: at what hour it is asked, the specific qualities involved, the "house" <note>Refers to the twelve Astrological Houses which govern different aspects of life, such as wealth, travel, or health.</note> of the question, and what signs are produced by the movement of that hour. One should fear the hour <unclear>ndta</unclear> and consider the proper hours of the earth and their colors. One must also observe the appearance of the celestial bodies: the sky should be clear and bright, not windy, cloudy, or rainy. Consider diligently the hour and the position of the Moon. It is good to work in the 2nd, 8th, and 11th hours; the 3rd, 5th, and 4th are <unclear>utert</unclear>; the 1st and 6th are vacant. Working in the 4th or 3rd is not useful, and the 10th is vacant. <unclear>perst uo. 12. t per midez pricias quo tro T 15 18 7 20</unclear>. On the first day, and on the 28th and 30th days, when you wish to work, if the Moon is in **Capricorn** or **Scorpio**, it is not useful and hinders the work. Constant practice leads to the spreading of prophecies. Before beginning, a promised prayer between the seeker and the master should be performed. These are numbers 8, 10, 11, 14, 21, 22.

<meta>This page transitions from the physical and temperament-based descriptions of planetary "children" to practical astronomical instructions for calculating the Moon's position in the zodiac.</meta>

If you want to know in which sign the Moon is at midday and how many signs, <term>degrees</term> <note>original: "staffel," literally "steps" or "rungs," referring here to the 30 degrees that make up one zodiac sign</note>, and minutes it has passed through, you should search in the table for the year of our Lord Jesus Christ; and what you find there are the signs, degrees, and minutes. Keep these on a slate or a table in peace, and these same signs, degrees, and minutes are called <term>roots</term> <note>original: "wurtzen," from the Latin "radix," referring to the base astronomical values used as a starting point for calculations</note>. After this, go into the calendar and take, for the day you desire to know, also the signs, degrees, and minutes, and add them to the previous calculation that you saved before. Add each together: the signs to the signs, degrees to degrees, and minutes to minutes. And if the minutes are more than **60**, then cast **60** away and add one degree to the degrees. If the degrees are more than **30**, then cast **30** away and add one sign to the signs. If there are **12** or more signs, then cast **12** away, and what remains are the signs, degrees, and minutes that the Moon has passed through at midday. And you should begin to count the signs at the Ram [Aries] where the symbol <image-desc>astrological symbol for Aries</image-desc> stands. And if it is one sign, then the Moon has run through the Ram, and so on.

If it is a leap year, however, there are two roots: the first lasts from the beginning of the year until St. Matthias's Day <note>February 24th, the traditional date for the leap year's additional day in the medieval calendar</note>, <insert>the second</insert> from then on. And that is briefly said concerning the Moon’s course.

It is also to be known that the roots last for **16** years; and when they expire, add to each root three degrees and **32** minutes and calculate it together. When that is done, they will last again for **16** years, and so on. Thus, in the year **1440**, there were roots and **2** signs and **22** degrees and **12** minutes, and so on for the others.

Now that you know in which sign the Moon is, if you then want to know when the Moon entered that sign, take the degrees that you calculated together through which the Moon has run at midday, and look for those same degrees in this following written table in the first <insert>lines</insert> lines where you find the degrees | there you will also find...

<meta>This page continues the astronomical instructions for tracking the Moon's movement through the zodiac signs and begins a section on "planetary hours," a form of electional astrology used to determine the best times for specific activities.</meta>

Write down the day, hour, and minute and subtract the Sun’s position from it, counting from midday; and wherever the calculation ends, that is when the Moon entered the zodiac sign.

Now, if you wish to know when the Moon moves from its current sign into the following sign, calculate how many <term>degrees</term> <note>original: "staffel," literally "steps," referring to the 30 degrees of a zodiac sign</note> the Moon has traveled through at midday. However many degrees there are less than 30, look for that number in the table written below. Search in the first column where it says "degrees," and where you find that degree, you will also find to the right hand the day, hour, and minute.

In **Saturn's** hour: do not begin a medical treatment <note>original: "arznije," likely referring to taking a potion or starting a cure</note>, do not separate any young livestock, and do not put on new clothes. Do not shave the head or the beard. Do not approach kings or princes. Do not seek out thieves. Do not travel by ship. Do not hire servants or maidens, and do not undertake any business, for it is a day of much talk <note>original: "gesprüch tag," implying a day wasted in idle chatter or dispute</note>. Do not go rowing or diving, and do not cross fields or water. However, you may well seek out your enemies, trap women, dig pits, and plow the earth.

---

In **Jupiter's** hour: perform marriages <note>original: "mach e," an archaic term for entering into the state of matrimony</note>, mine for ore, weave cloth, and make new clothes. Go out into the field and travel by water, even across the sea. Build granaries <note>original: "hörn"</note> and other structures like <term>lunar houses</term> <note>original: "lunus hüser," likely referring to buildings aligned with the mansions of the moon</note>. Do not buy hair or horses, nor livestock or birds. Do not travel by ship on the water.

---

In **Mars's** hour: undertake nothing at all on this earth, and be fearful of all things at this time.

---

In the **Sun's** hour: all things are unlucky except for approaching princes and lords. Also, whatever is done before the sun [rises] and goes out is good. You may well go out and rob, as it is a time for wicked deeds. Go out hunting, and accept offices and honors.

---

In **Venus's** hour: concern yourself with courtship <note>original: "pul," meaning a lover or paramour</note> and physical love, and perform marriages. Drink medicines and take <term>purgatives</term> <note>treatments used to cleanse the digestive system</note>. Go out into the field for everything that is profitable. Do not approach kings or princes. Do not go to the baths or for <term>cupping</term> <note>original: "ventusen," the practice of applying heated glass cups to the skin to draw out "bad humors"</note>. Do not engage in strife or speak of old matters.

# The Ram

<image-desc>Large decorative red initial O with fine scrollwork filling the counter</image-desc>
**O**f the twelve signs, their nature and properties:
The first is **Aries** <note>the Ram; original: "wider"</note>, which is a fire sign, fiery and dry by nature. It is the house of **Mars** and the exaltation of the **Sun**. It governs the head, the face, the eyes, and whatever is on the head of a person. When the man <note>referring to the Moon's position in the "Zodiac Man," a medical diagram mapping signs to body parts</note> is in Aries, it is not good to treat the head with medicine, nor to touch the parts of the head with iron <note>surgical tools or blades</note>. It is also not good to shave the beard or wash the head. It is good to travel from place to place, especially toward the East. It is good for bloodletting, for cutting open wounds, for planting and sowing in the soil, for traveling, and for putting on new clothes. Everything is good to do that involves fire and anything that should reach a quick conclusion. It is good for cupping and bathing; and if someone becomes sick now, they will soon be healthy again. However, those things which are firm and long-lasting are not good to begin. If something is lost, it will soon and gladly be found again—provided that the man is not hindered by other planets or stars. The same is to be understood for the signs described hereafter.

## Taurus

<image-desc>Large decorative red initial D with a stylized floral or geometric motif inside</image-desc>
**D****Taurus** <note>the Bull; original: "stier"</note> is a sign of the earth, cold and dry by nature. This sign governs the neck, the glands, the throat <note>original: "kropf," often referring to a goiter or swelling</note>, and all sicknesses of the neck. When the man is in this sign, it is not good to disturb the aforementioned limbs with medicine. It is good to do and to begin all things that should remain stable and firm and last a long time, such as lifelong partnerships. It is good for building houses and making peace between enemies. It is good to begin a war as a knight, or for any matter that should not last long. It is not good to begin a long journey, but small and short trips are usually good. It is not good to cut wounds or to bleed, nor to take medicine. Things that are lost now will seldom return. Whoever becomes sick now will only become healthy with difficulty <note>original: "anle," likely a contraction for "unlange" or similar, implying a long recovery</note>. It is not good to carry out or engage in courtly affairs <note>original: "hoffmanschatz," referring to the pursuits or treasures of a courtier</note>, especially toward midday. Taurus is the exaltation of the **Moon** <note>original: "mānz"</note> and the house of **Venus**, and therefore they have power here.

# Gemini

**Gemini** <note>the Twins; original: "zwilung"</note> is a sign of the East <note>original: "orient"</note>, of the nature of air, warm and moist. It is of a good, mild temperament and governs the shoulders, the arms, the shoulder blades, and the hands. When the Moon <note>original: "mane"</note> is in this sign, it is not good to treat the aforementioned limbs with medicine or to touch them with iron—such as for surgery—and therefore it is very bad and dangerous to let blood <note>original: "ader lassen," referring to phlebotomy</note> from the arms. This is because it often happens that the bloodletter must strike a muscle <note>original: "mus," which could refer to a muscle, tendon, or nerve</note>, and it may happen that the arms swell. If the bloodletter strikes a muscle, a person may even die from it, or become very sick, or the arms may become lame and unresponsive, as if they were asleep. It is also not good to form alliances, nor to enter into contracts or praise companions, for the sign is unstable. It is not good to put on new clothes. It is also not good to travel, and whatever one begins then tends to be divided against itself <note>original: "zwispelt," implying that the effort will split, double, or fail to remain unified</note>. It is good to travel by land if the distance is not great, especially toward the East, but it is bad to travel over water. If a person falls sick during this time, it happens easily. If a person is found <note>likely referring to a lost person or a fugitive</note>, they will likely become sick. If a prisoner is released briefly, they will soon be captured again,

for the sign is the house of **Mercury**.

# The Lion

<note>Leo</note>

The Lion <note>Leo</note> is a sign of the East <note>original: "orient"</note>, of the nature of fire, hot, fiery, and dry. It governs the stomach, the sides, the heart, the back, and whatever is formed in that region. It is good to speak with princes and with great lords, and it is good to do whatever must be done with fire, such as the casting of bells. It is good to begin what should last a long time, such as building with timber. It is good to begin far-reaching enterprises and to do weighty things. It is bad to begin long journeys, or to put on new clothes, or to bleed <note>original: "lassen," referring to phlebotomy or bloodletting</note>, or to take medicinal drinks <note>purgatives</note>, or to practice other medicine. The Lion is the house of the Sun, and it has great power therein.

Indeed, it is good for no one. It is not good to begin long voyages by ship. The Maid is the exaltation of Mercury and also his house, and therefore he has great power in it.

...when the Moon <note>original: "mān," likely a transcription for "mân" (Moon)</note> is in this sign [Capricorn], it is not good to treat with medicine or to shave <note>original: "scheren," referring to the cutting of hair or shaving of the skin for medical prep</note> the aforementioned limbs <note>Capricorn governs the knees</note>. It is good to call upon the authorities <note>original: ".k.", an abbreviation for "Könige" (kings) or "Kaiser" (emperors)</note>. It is good [to travel] toward the East <note>original: "orient"</note> for short journeys, but long journeys are not good. This sign is the house of Saturn, and therefore when the Moon is in this sign, it has great power—even greater than the Moon typically has in Capricorn.

## Pisces

**Pisces** is a sign of the North <note>original: "septemtrion"</note>, of a watery nature, cold and moist. It is a sign that stands for itself <note>likely referring to its independent nature or its status as a "double" sign</note> and governs the feet, the toes, and the area from the feet to the ankles. When the Moon is in this sign, it is not good to treat the aforementioned limbs with medicine or to cauterize them with iron. It is good to seek after friendship, to call upon the authorities, and to exchange coins, silver, and gold for profit. It is particularly good to travel toward the North and to journey there. It is good to protect, organize, and arrange matters. It is good to perform any task that involves water. It is good to take medicinal drinks <note>original: "trenker," potions or tonics</note> and it is good to put on new clothes. It is also a favorable time to let blood from the veins and it is good to treat <note>original: "schmidē," likely meaning to salve or perform surgery</note> wounds on the feet. This sign is the exaltation <note>original: "erhöhūg," a planetary position of maximum strength</note> of Venus, and therefore it has great power within it.

And this is a brief account of the nature and properties of the twelve signs as the masters <note>referring to authoritative ancient and medieval astrologers</note> have written of them. And what is said here is most likely to occur when the sign rises in the East; if it should happen otherwise, it is due to the influence of the other planets, about which there would be much to write, but for the sake of brevity I shall leave it be.

# Properties or <gloss>accidents</gloss> <note>In medieval medicine, "accidents" refer to non-essential qualities or symptoms of a substance.</note> of the blood
## which the human has within them

<margin>Good [characteristics] of the blood itself <note>original Latin: "Bonum proprio sanguinia"</note></margin>
Blood which is neither too thick nor too thin <note>original: "subtil"</note>, but is also friable or soft; red in color, mild in taste, with a little water on top—this is praiseworthy and natural.

<margin>Concerning yellow bile <note>original Latin: "proprio colera"</note></margin>
However, that which is far too thin, very red and murky or sharp <note>original: "lur oder klug"</note>, yellow and bitter with a strong and bitter aftertaste <note>original: "ach"</note>—that is bad. It comes from a moisture, and that moisture is called cholera <note>yellow bile</note>. It is hot in nature and makes the person angry.

<margin>Concerning melancholy <note>original Latin: "proprio melancholica"</note></margin>
Also, when the blood is thick in its substance, black with very little red, mixed with yellow, and in taste a little sour or vinegary—that is bad and coarse. It comes from [cold] and dry moisture <note>In the humoral system, melancholy or black bile was characterized as cold and dry.</note> called melancholy. From this, the person is heavy-minded <note>melancholic or depressed</note>.

<margin>Concerning phlegm <note>original Latin: "proprio flegma"</note></margin>
Also, blood that is thick and white-watery, sweet in taste—this is coarse and comes from the moisture of phlegm, from which the person expectorates <note>original: "uswirft," literally "throws out" or coughs up</note> much and is sluggish <note>original: "unfläng," meaning listless or unclean</note>.

Also, blood that contains much urine and water signifies a great weakness of the kidneys, or results from the many kinds of drinking that the person does.

Also, to drive away a <term>splint</term> <note>original: "über bein"; a bony growth or exostosis on a horse's leg</note> in a horse: in the evening when you wish to go to sleep, eat two or three mouthfuls of cheese. And in the morning when you wake up, take your fasting <term>saliva</term> <note>original: "speicher"; "fasting spittle" (saliva collected before eating) was a common ingredient in folk medicine, believed to possess special healing properties</note> into a bowl and put a spoonful of <term>mustard seed</term> therein. Then, shave the hair off the horse and clean the <term>injury</term> <note>original: "schade"</note>, and rub it well with <term>beef tallow</term> <note>original: "rinderin vngschlit"; rendered beef fat used as a base for salves</note>. Then bind the mixture over it and fasten it well with a piece of leather so that it does not fall off. Let that stay for three days and three nights. On the third day, <term>bathe</term> <note>original: "hūro"; likely a dialect variant of "huren" or "wash/treat"</note> the horse with warm <term>elder</term> <note>original: "fliedern"; likely elderflower or elderberry water</note> and wash it well with wine. Then take <term>pike jawbones</term> <note>original: "hecht kinnbagge"</note> and burn them in a pot and crush them into a powder; strew that into the wound, and the horse will recover. -/-

Also, if you want to drive away <term>joint fluid</term> <note>original: "lidwasser"; likely referring to a synovial effusion, windgalls, or "water on the joint"</note>, take an egg white and <term>alum</term> <note>original: "alat"; a mineral salt used as an astringent</note>. Stir the egg white with the alum until it foams and put it into a container. Smear the injury with this and it will pass away. -/-

Also, for <term>inflammation</term> <note>original: "brand"; this term could refer to a burn, a localized infection, or even gangrene ("the fire")</note>, take lime that is <term>unslaked</term> <note>Quicklime, which reacts heat-intensively with water</note> and pour spring water onto it nine times. Stir it well together each time and always let it settle. When it has settled well, pour the water off the lime. On the ninth time, take the lime and put <term>linseed oil</term> and <term>breast milk</term> <note>original: "frawen milch"</note> into it. Anoint the inflammation with this and the horse will recover. -/-

Also, if you want to drive away <term>spots</term> <note>original: "fletke"; likely referring to cataracts or corneal scarring</note> in an eye, take the root of <term>lovage</term> <note>original: "lüsterus"; likely a corruption of Levisticum (lovage), a common herb in medieval veterinary manuals</note> and bind it to the neck for nine days, and the spot will pass away. -/-

# January

The thunder that comes in January signifies
hardship and strong winds, an abundance of grain,
unrest, and <term>war</term> <note>original: "urlig"; an archaic term for war or conflict</note> among the people.

The thunder that comes in **February** <note>original: "Hornung"; the traditional German name for February, referring to the "shedding of horns" or the month's brevity</note> signifies
diseases and death among the people, and most especially among the rich.

The thunder that comes in March heralds
strong winds, enough grain, and strife among the
people. **March**

The thunder in April signifies [good] vines and **April**
enough grain. **May**

The thunder in May heralds little grain,
poverty, much hunger, and many kinds of
sicknesses. **June** <note>original: "Brachar"; the fallow month, traditionally June</note>

The thunder in June heralds enough grain
and many kinds of sicknesses. **July** <note>original: "Huwmanot"; the hay month, traditionally July</note>

The thunder in July heralds good <term>fodder</term> <note>original: "fůrŭg"; refers to pasturage or winter feed for livestock</note>.

--- Page 217 ---
<meta>This page continues the medical and astrological guidance from the previous section. While the previous page focused on the Zodiac signs, this page provides a "Regimen Sanitatis" (a Regimen of Health), offering specific dietary, hygienic, and bloodletting instructions for each month of the year, beginning in January.</meta>

# January

In this month, you shall not let blood <note>original: "sanguinem non minuabis," the practice of phlebotomy to balance the body's fluids</note> because of the extreme cold. Warmth is sent into the blood of the body. Take sweet electuaries <note>medicinal pastes or lozenges</note>; take each of them as they are required. Consume hot things throughout January to stay healthy. The Egyptian days <note>unlucky days on the medieval calendar, also called "dies mali"</note> ought to be observed throughout the year. In this month, blood is not to be diminished, nor should a purging potion be taken.

---

# February

February is named after *februde*, that is, purification <note>referring to the Roman festival of Februa</note>, or from *fribus*, meaning oats, as if from the cold. They say that in February one should bear the salt of the rains <unclear>ebrius</unclear>. In this month, do not eat beets, for they contain poison. Use gargles and Oxymel <term>Oxymel: a traditional medicinal syrup made of honey and vinegar, believed to thin the humors</term> so that it may lead out the bile, phlegm, and melancholy through the bowels. Take foods that digest well; take them while fasting. Do not neglect to beware of the cold here. Draw blood from the thumb, but for a successful purging, take a drink; for all people, a small bloodletting is good. A good potion is agrimony or celery seed.

---

# March

In this month, use a bath after eating roasted meats. Do not draw blood. Do not drink water. Let the fasting person eat sweet things. Drink sweet, unmixed wine and eat radish roots prepared in honey and vinegar until you are satisfied. In the morning, let him eat; drink a full cup of warm water and immediately put a feather dipped in oil or a finger into the throat, and by moving it thus, provoke vomiting <note>inducing vomiting was a common method of purging "corrupt" humors from the stomach</note>. Do not take laxatives <note>original: "soluciones"</note>, because the purging itself produces cold. Drink and chew pennyroyal <note>original: "polegium"</note>. Let the potion be of rue and lily-bulbs <note>original: "libris," possibly referring to a weight measurement or the herb 'lilium'</note>.

---

# April

In this month, let blood from the median vein <note>the large vein in the crook of the elbow</note> because of pain. Let him eat fresh meats; abstain from roots. Use warm things. For pain of the stomach, purge with a vigorous laxative. Let the blood be diminished <note>let blood</note> and purge the urine. Let the potion be pimpernel and betony, <gloss>but</gloss> one must beware of purging <insert>releasing</insert> <note>the word "solvendi" is struck through in red ink in the original</note>. From this time until the middle of July, washings <note>enemas or baths</note> should be given through the lower parts so that the heat does not cause an obstruction. In this month, if it should thunder while the sky is clear, it signifies a pestilence.

---

# May

With these previous things having been done, use these species: in this month, you should eat the head or extremities of no animal, because all the poisons are rising. Know that you should not drink water while fasting. Let blood from the head vein. Drink warm things and use warm preparations. Take a purging potion; eat a handful of chervil <note>original: "decerefolia," likely cerefolium</note> while fasting. Cleanse the itch with cold vegetables and vinegar; drink agrimony and yarrow <note>original: "millefolium"</note>. It is good to sleep. If it thunders at night, it notes sickness. All things [concerning the feast of] St. Florian.

**Technical Terms:**
bloodletting <note>original: "sanguinem minuere"</note>, medicinal pastes <note>original: "electuaria"</note>, gargles <note>original: "gargarismos"</note>, honey-vinegar syrup <note>original: "oximel"</note>, pimpernel <note>original: "pimpinella"</note>, betony <note>original: "betonia"</note>, agrimony <note>original: "agrimonia"</note>, yarrow <note>original: "millefolium"</note>, unlucky days <note>original: "dies egypciaci"</note>, health regimen <note>original: "regimen sanitatis"</note>.

<meta>This page continues the "Regimen Sanitatis" (Health Regimen) from the previous section. The previous page concluded with March. This page skips April and May, resuming with June, and provides dietary, botanical, and bloodletting instructions for the remainder of the year. The month names used here are Latinized versions of Old Germanic names.</meta>

### June <note>original: "Brachot," from the German "Brachmonat," the month for plowing fallow fields</note>

In this month, you should not let blood <note>original: "sanguine non minuas," referring to phlebotomy</note> and you should not take a loosening potion <note>a purgative or laxative used to clear the bowels</note>. Do not be deceived by a cup of cold water; instead, drink wormwood every day while fasting. Drink warm liquids and take ordinary vinegar, mead <note>original: "medone," a fermented honey drink</note>, and a decoction of hawthorn. Let your medicinal drink be made of sage and savory <note>original: "sanyna," likely a corruption of satureia</note>. Eat lettuce leaves with fruit. Drink from fresh springs.

### July <note>original: "Höwmānot," from "Heumonat," the hay-harvest month</note>

In this month, purgings and floury foods are troublesome. Stay far away from the acts of Venus <note>sexual intercourse</note>, because at this time the brain produces excess humors. Do not take a purging potion; you may drink cold water and elderflowers, but where a warm potion is required, let it be rue, celery, and cooked wine. Do not harm the veins <note>avoid bloodletting</note>. Believe that these herbs are helpful now: Germander, cumin, and sage.

### August <note>original: "Östte," likely a variant of "Austmonat," the harvest month</note>

In this month, one must avoid hot foods, as they are harmful. Do not eat cabbage stalks nor mallows, because they are bitter and turn into black bile <term>Black Bile: in medieval medicine, one of the four humors (melancholy) which, if out of balance, caused illness and depression</term>. Do not eat... <unclear>comedone</unclear> and do not drink decoctions. Do not let blood. For your health, eat <unclear>acmen</unclear> and drink wormwood and pennyroyal. A potion is good, but bloodletting is not. You should not eat geese.

### September <note>original: "Herbst," meaning the autumn or harvest month</note>

At this time, strike the vein <note>bloodletting is permitted again</note> and diligently use these spices. Eat morsels of bread soaked in goat’s milk every day while fasting. Because every bird and all things are mature and perfect at this time, you may eat them. Incise the vein of the sides and the liver vein <term>Liver vein: known as the "vena hepatica," located in the arm and believed to treat liver-related ailments</term>. Let your medicinal drink be costmary <note>original: "costa"</note> and agrimony <note>original: "agnomalstria"</note>.

### October <note>original: "Wimmānot," from "Weinmonat," the wine-pressing month</note>

In this month, it is good to eat clusters of grapes and to drink must <note>unfermented grape juice</note>, because it loosens the bowels and heals the body. However, eat your leeks cooked; raw leeks are like poison, but cooked they are worthy of health. Take blood from the cephalic vein <term>Cephalic vein: the "head vein" in the arm, traditionally bled to treat issues above the neck</term> in the arm.
<margin>from which the pain of the head and the watering of the eyes are relieved <unclear>p p cario fila lac ut ouia m</unclear></margin>

### November <note>original: "Harmanot"</note>

In this month, incise the head vein, the liver vein, and the cephalic vein. Abstain from baths and from eating cabbage stalks. Do not eat the heads of animals. Use these spices: cinnamon, nard <note>original: "spica," an aromatic Himalayan plant</note>, and ginger. Some say that it is good to let blood when the moon is in the north; others say that it is only good to let blood between the 5th and the 25th day of the moon. Generally, however, do not let blood on the first day of a new moon, lest a "flux of the belly" <note>diarrhea</note> or a long fever follow you.

### December <note>original: "Wintmanot," the winter month</note>

Warm things are suitable for the limbs in the month of December. Abstain from cabbage. Take a medicinal potion. Incise the head vein. Eat warm foods. Let the potion be made with nard.

<meta>This page transitions from the technical astronomical tables of the previous page to a series of prognostications. While the previous pages provided the mathematical tools to track the Moon, this text applies such chronological data—specifically the day of the week on which the year begins—to predict the harvest, weather, and social outcomes for the year ahead.</meta>

If the <note>original: "festum Ianuarii"</note> feast of January should fall on a **Sunday**, the winter will be good, the spring windy, and the summer dry. The vintage will be good, cattle will thrive, and sheep will grow and multiply. Honey will be abundant; old men will die, and there shall be peace.

$\P$ If it be on a **Monday**, the winter will be mixed with winds and good weather. The summer will be dry and windy, and there will be storms. The vintage will not be good; many men and bees will die. There will be a flood of waters; grain will be plentiful, but honey will be scarce. There will be wars of men and princes.

$\P$ If it be on a **Tuesday**, the winter will be rainy and windy; the spring will be windy and rainy. The summer will be dry and the vintage laborious. The autumn will be good. Many <note>original: "momā," likely "morbos" or "mortes"</note> diseases or deaths will occur; judges and kings shall perish. Honey will be abundant.

$\P$ If it be on a **Wednesday**, the winter will be hard and harsh, both bad and windy. The summer will be good and warm. The vintage will be good but laborious; the autumn and the grain will be good. In the end, [many] shall die; sailors shall labor excessively. There will be some <term>pains of the belly</term> <note>original: "ventris solo"</note> and many pains of the <term>midriff</term> <note>original: "precordiorum," referring to the internal organs or the area around the heart.</note>.

$\P$ If it be on a **Thursday**, the winter will be good and the spring windy. The summer will be good and the vintage copious. Kings, sheep, and bees will die. There will be many rains, the rivers will be cold, and there will be wars and dangers among men.

$\P$ If it be on a **Friday**, the winter will be changeable but windy and good. The summer will be dry and not good. There will be pain in the eyes. The vintage will be copious, but the grain harvest will be a struggle. Sheep shall perish and navigation will be difficult. There will be hail and coughing. <insert>Oil</insert> will be abundant. Kings shall perish and many men will die.

$\P$ If it be on a **Saturday**, the winter will be bad and windy. All fruits will be difficult to harvest. Sheep shall perish and old men will die. Many houses will be burned.
